easy.def: For everyone to use.
examples: A public park is open.
A public library is free.
The beach is public.

more.def: Open to all people, not private.
examples: The public library lends books to everyone.
A public park is open to the whole town.
The pool is public on Saturdays.

easy.def: People in general.
examples: The museum is open to the public.
The public can visit.
The park is for the public.

more.def: People in general, as a group.
examples: The zoo is open to the public every day.
The mayor spoke to the public.
Announcements were made for the public.

easy.def: A book or magazine that is printed for people to read.
examples: This is a new publication.
The library has many publications.
A school publication.

more.def: A book, magazine or newspaper that has been printed and made available to the public, or the act of printing it.
examples: The school's weekly publication included stories written by students.
The library has publications about space and animals.
The publication of the new book was a big event in town.

easy.def: Attention from the public.
examples: The show got a lot of publicity.
The publicity helped sales.
The new store needed publicity.

more.def: News and information that make many people know about something.
examples: The new movie got a lot of publicity.
The fair used posters for publicity.
The publicity brought many visitors.

easy.def: To print and sell books or news.
examples: They publish books.
The newspaper published the story.
She published a book.

more.def: To print and sell a book, magazine or news so that people can read it.
examples: The company published my favorite book.
The newspaper published the story on Friday.
She published a book about whales.

related.def: A company or person that publishes books.

easy.def: The business of making and selling books and magazines.
examples: She works in publishing.
Publishing makes books.
He wants to work in publishing.

more.def: The business of preparing and selling books, magazines and other printed works.
examples: My aunt works in publishing and helps make children's books.
The publishing company printed thousands of copies of the book.
He wants a job in publishing when he grows up.

easy.def: The flat black disk used in hockey.
examples: He hit the puck.
The puck slid on the ice.
She passed the puck.

more.def: The small, flat, round piece of hard rubber that players hit with sticks in ice hockey.
examples: The player flicked the puck across the ice into the goal.
The goalkeeper stopped the puck with her pad.
The puck slid across the ice and hit the wall.

easy.def: To squeeze your lips together.
examples: I pucker my lips.
He puckered at the lemon.
She puckered up.

more.def: To pull the lips or cloth into small folds, often when tasting something sour.
examples: The sour lemon made me pucker.
She puckered her lips to blow a kiss.
His mouth puckered at the sour candy.

easy.def: A soft, sweet dessert.
examples: I eat pudding.
The pudding is chocolate.
Mom made pudding.

more.def: A soft, creamy dessert that is often eaten with a spoon.
examples: We had chocolate pudding for dessert.
The pudding was smooth and sweet.
Mom spooned pudding into little cups.

easy.def: A small pool of water on the ground.
examples: I jumped in a puddle.
A puddle formed after the rain.
The dog splashed in the puddle.

more.def: A small, shallow pool of water or other liquid on the ground, often left after rain.
examples: I splashed through the puddle in my new rain boots.
After the storm, big puddles filled the road.
A puddle of milk spread across the kitchen floor.

easy.def: A small cloud of air or smoke.
examples: A puff of wind blew.
I saw a puff of smoke.
The puff of air was cool.

more.def: A short, light burst of air, smoke or steam.
examples: A puff of wind blew my hat off.
A puff of steam rose from the kettle.
The train made puffs of white smoke.

easy.def: To blow out air in short bursts.
examples: I puff on the candle.
The engine puffed.
She puffed up the hill.

more.def: To blow out air in short bursts, or to swell up.
examples: The little engine puffed up the hill.
I puffed out my cheeks.
The runner puffed after the race.

easy.def: Breathing hard, or giving out puffs.
examples: The puffing train left the station.
A puffing runner.
The puffing steam rose.

more.def: Breathing hard, or sending out small clouds of smoke or steam.
examples: The puffing engine pulled the cars up the hill.
The puffing runner stopped to rest.
Puffing smoke rose from the chimney.

easy.def: Swollen or round and soft.
examples: A puffy cloud.
My eye is puffy.
A puffy jacket.

more.def: Round, soft and a little swollen, like a puffed-up cloud or a pillow.
examples: Puffy white clouds floated across the blue sky.
My eyes were puffy from crying.
She wore a puffy jacket to keep warm.

easy.def: A small dog with a flat face and curly tail.
examples: The pug snored.
I have a pug.
The pug has a flat face.

more.def: A small dog with a wrinkled, flat face and a curled tail.
examples: The pug snored loudly on the couch.
A pug has a flat face and a curly tail.
Our neighbor's pug waddled down the sidewalk.

easy.def: To move something toward you.
examples: Pull the door.
He pulled the wagon.
I pull the rope.

more.def: To take hold of something and move it toward you or after you.
examples: Please pull the door instead of pushing it.
The horses pulled the wagon up the hill.
She pulled a weed out of the garden.

easy.def: A wheel with a rope that helps lift heavy things.
examples: The pulley lifts the bucket.
A pulley has a wheel.
We used a pulley.

more.def: A wheel with a rope or chain over it that makes it easier to lift heavy things.
examples: The farmer used a pulley to raise the hay.
A pulley lifted the bucket from the well.
The flag goes up on a pulley.

easy.def: The soft inside of a fruit, or a soft wet mass.
examples: Orange juice has pulp.
The pulp is soft.
The fruit is full of pulp.

more.def: The soft, juicy inside of a fruit, or a soft, wet mass of crushed wood used to make paper.
examples: I like orange juice with lots of pulp.
The soft pulp of the apple was sweet.
Paper is made from wood pulp.

easy.def: A small raised stand where a speaker stands in church.
examples: The speaker stood at the pulpit.
The pulpit is wood.
A pulpit is high.

more.def: A raised platform or stand in a church from which a person speaks.
examples: The speaker stood at the pulpit to talk.
A wooden pulpit stood at the front of the church.
He climbed the steps to the pulpit.

easy.def: The beat of your heart that you can feel in your wrist.
examples: The nurse felt my pulse.
My pulse is fast after running.
I felt my pulse in my neck.

more.def: The steady beat of blood pushed through your body by your heart, which you can feel in your wrist or neck.
examples: The nurse counted my pulse for one minute.
Your pulse speeds up when you run.
I put my fingers on my wrist to find my pulse.

easy.def: A machine that moves water or air.
examples: We use a pump to put air in the tire.
The pump brings water to the house.
Dad used a pump for the ball.

more.def: A machine or tool that moves water, air or other liquids from one place to another.
examples: I used a bike pump to fill the tire with air.
The pump moves water up from the well.
A fire truck has a strong pump.

easy.def: To move water or air with a machine.
examples: Pump the water.
I pumped air into the ball.
He pumps the tire.

more.def: To push air or liquid along in a steady flow, as a machine or a heart does.
examples: She pumped up the bike tire.
The heart pumps blood all around the body.
The farmer pumped water into the trough.

easy.def: A big, round, orange vegetable.
examples: We carved a pumpkin.
The pumpkin is orange.
I grew a pumpkin.

more.def: A large, round, orange fruit that grows on a vine and is used for pies and Halloween lanterns.
examples: We carved a pumpkin for Halloween.
Mom made a pie from the pumpkin.
The pumpkins ripen in the fall.

easy.def: To hit with your fist.
examples: He punched the pillow.
Do not punch.
The boxer punches.

more.def: To hit something with a closed hand.
examples: The boxer punched the bag.
He punched the pillow to make it fluffy.
She punched a button on the machine.

easy.def: To make a hole in paper.
examples: Punch holes in the paper.
The ticket was punched.
She punches holes.

more.def: To make a hole in something with a tool.
examples: Punch two holes in the paper for the folder.
The conductor punched my ticket.
She punched holes in the lid.

easy.def: A sweet fruit drink.
examples: We drank fruit punch.
The punch is red.
There is punch at the party.

more.def: A sweet drink made from fruit juices.
examples: We drank cold fruit punch at the party.
The punch bowl was full of red juice.
Mom served punch at the picnic.

easy.def: On time.
examples: She is punctual.
The bus is punctual.
Be punctual for school.

more.def: Arriving at the time that was set, not late.
examples: The bus is always punctual in the morning.
She is punctual and never late for class.
A punctual train pulled into the station at noon.

easy.def: Being on time.
examples: Punctuality is good.
Her punctuality is great.
He is known for punctuality.

more.def: The habit of being on time.
examples: Her punctuality means she is never late for class.
Punctuality is important for catching a train.
The coach praised the team's punctuality.

easy.def: A tiny hole made by something sharp.
examples: The tire has a puncture.
A thorn made a puncture.
He fixed the puncture in his bike tire.

more.def: A small hole made by something sharp, especially one that lets air out of a tire or ball.
examples: A nail made a puncture in the bike tire, and the air slowly leaked out.
Dad patched the puncture in the rubber raft.
The doctor put a small bandage over the tiny puncture.

easy.def: To make a tiny hole in something.
examples: A thorn punctured the tire.
Don't puncture the ball.
The nail punctured my shoe.

more.def: To make a small hole in something with a sharp point.
examples: A sharp rock punctured the bottom of the boat.
Be careful not to puncture the balloon with the pin.
She punctured the foil lid with a fork before putting the dish in the oven.

easy.def: To make someone have a bad result for doing wrong.
examples: Mom did not punish me.
The teacher punishes cheating.
They punished the player.

more.def: To give someone a penalty for something they did wrong.
examples: The coach punished the team by making them run extra laps.
It is not fair to punish a child for something they did not do.
The judge punished the thief.

easy.def: Able to get a penalty.
examples: Cheating is punishable.
It is a punishable act.
The rule says it is punishable.

more.def: Able to be punished by a penalty or loss of something.
examples: Cheating in the game is punishable by losing points.
Breaking the rules is punishable.
The school says leaving early is punishable.

easy.def: What happens to you for doing something wrong.
examples: The punishment was fair.
Her punishment was to clean up.
A punishment taught him a lesson.

more.def: A penalty that is given to someone who has done something wrong.
examples: His punishment for being rude was to say sorry.
A fair punishment teaches a lesson without being cruel.
The coach said running laps was not a punishment, but practice.

easy.def: To drop a ball and kick it before it hits the ground.
examples: He will punt the ball.
She punted the football.
The player punted.

more.def: To kick a ball that you have dropped from your hands before it touches the ground.
examples: The player punted the football down the field.
He punted the ball high into the air.
She punted the ball over the fence.

easy.def: A kick of a ball dropped from your hands.
examples: He kicked a punt.
The punt was high.
A long punt flew.

more.def: A kick in which a player drops the ball and kicks it before it touches the ground.
examples: He kicked a long punt down the field.
The punt sailed over the goalpost.
Her punt flew nearly forty yards.

easy.def: Small and weak.
examples: A puny plant.
The puny chick.
His puny arm.

more.def: Small and weak, or very small in size or amount.
examples: The puny plant barely grew in the shade.
A puny chick peeped from the nest.
The puny fire gave almost no heat.

easy.def: A young dog.
examples: The pup plays with me.
The pup is small.
We got a new pup.

more.def: A young dog, or the young of some other animals, such as seals and wolves.
examples: The pup chewed on its toy bone.
A seal pup lay on the rocks beside its mother.
We watched the pups tumble and play in the yard.

easy.def: A student.
examples: The pupil raised her hand.
The pupils lined up.
A new pupil joined the class.

more.def: A child who goes to school and is taught by a teacher.
examples: A pupil from the next class lent me a pencil.
The pupils lined up for lunch.
A new pupil joined our class.

easy.def: The black center of your eye.
examples: The pupil is black.
The pupil gets bigger in the dark.
The pupil is round.

more.def: The small, round, black opening in the middle of the eye that lets in light.
examples: The pupil of your eye gets bigger in the dark.
The cat's pupil was a thin slit.
The doctor shone a light in her pupil.

easy.def: A toy you move with your hand.
examples: I play with a puppet.
The puppet has a face.
The puppet show was fun.

more.def: A toy figure that you move with your hand or with strings.
examples: The puppet waved at the children.
I made a puppet from a sock.
The puppet show was funny.

easy.def: A person who moves puppets in a show.
examples: The puppeteer moved the puppet.
A puppeteer did a show.
I want to be a puppeteer.

more.def: A person who works puppets in a show.
examples: The puppeteer made the wooden puppet dance.
A puppeteer hid behind the stage and spoke in funny voices.
The puppeteers took a bow after the show.

easy.def: A young dog.
examples: The puppy is cute.
I have a new puppy.
The puppy chews my shoes.

more.def: A baby dog.
examples: The puppy chased its tail.
Our puppy is learning to sit.
The puppies slept in a pile.

easy.def: To buy something.
examples: I will purchase a ticket.
She purchased a book.
They purchased a car.

more.def: To buy something, usually something that costs a lot.
examples: I purchased two tickets for the show.
Dad purchased a new bike for my birthday.
She purchased a book at the store.

easy.def: Something you buy.
examples: I made a purchase.
The purchase was small.
The purchase was a hat.

more.def: Something that you have bought, or the act of buying it.
examples: The purchase of a new computer cost a lot.
She carried her purchases home in a bag.
Keep the receipt for your purchase.

easy.def: Clean, with nothing else mixed in.
examples: The water is pure.
This is pure gold.
The air in the mountains is pure.

more.def: Clean and clear, with nothing added or mixed in.
examples: The pure white snow sparkled in the sun.
The ring was made of pure gold.
The spring gives pure water.

related.def: A thing that makes something pure.

easy.def: To make clean and pure.
examples: We purify the water.
A filter purifies air.
Boil water to purify it.

more.def: To make something clean and pure by removing dirt or anything harmful.
examples: A filter purifies the water so that it is safe to drink.
Plants help to purify the air.
The town built a plant to purify the river water.

easy.def: Being clean and not mixed with anything else.
examples: The purity of the water is good.
The purity of the gold.
They tested the purity.

more.def: The state of being clean and not mixed with anything else.
examples: Scientists tested the purity of the lake water.
The purity of the gold made it very valuable.
The snow's purity sparkled in the sun.

easy.def: The color you get by mixing red and blue.
examples: The grapes are purple.
She wore a purple coat.
The flower is purple.

more.def: Having the color made by mixing red and blue.
examples: Purple grapes grew on the vine.
She painted the door purple.
The sunset turned the sky purple.

easy.def: A color between red and blue.
examples: Purple is my favorite color.
I like purple.
She chose purple.

more.def: The color that is made by mixing red and blue.
examples: The king wore purple on special days.
The artist mixed red and blue to make purple.
The robe was dyed a deep purple.

easy.def: The reason for something.
examples: What is the purpose of this tool?
The purpose is to help.
The purpose of the test.

more.def: The reason why something is done or made.
examples: The purpose of a fence is to keep the animals in.
The purpose of a lock is to keep things safe.
The purpose of the meeting is to plan the picnic.

easy.def: To make a soft, low humming sound, like a happy cat.
examples: The cat purred.
The kitten purrs.
The engine purred.

more.def: To make a soft, low, humming sound, as a happy cat does, or to run quietly, as an engine does.
examples: The cat purred happily in my lap.
The engine purred smoothly as we drove off.
The kitten purred when I scratched its ears.

easy.def: A soft, low humming sound.
examples: I heard a purr.
The cat's purr.
A quiet purr.

more.def: A soft, low humming sound that a cat makes when it is happy.
examples: We heard the soft purr of the cat.
The purr of the engine was quiet.
The kitten's purr made me smile.

easy.def: A small bag for money and small things.
examples: Mom put her keys in her purse.
The purse is red.
She opened her purse.

more.def: A small bag that holds money, keys and other small things.
examples: She tucked her wallet and her phone into her purse.
The girl kept her coins in a tiny purse.
She found a tissue in her purse.

easy.def: To chase after something.
examples: The dog pursued the ball.
The cat pursues a mouse.
We pursued the kite down the hill.

more.def: To follow or chase something in order to catch it, or to work toward a goal.
examples: The police car pursued the speeding truck.
She pursued her dream of becoming a doctor.
The lion pursued the zebra across the plain.

easy.def: Chasing something.
examples: The dog ran in pursuit of the ball.
The pursuit was long.
The police chased in pursuit.

more.def: The act of chasing after something, or working toward a goal.
examples: The pursuit of the stolen bike led to the park.
The pursuit of happiness is important.
The cat was in hot pursuit of the mouse.

easy.def: To press on something to make it move away.
examples: Push the door open.
I push the swing.
She pushed the cart.

more.def: To press against something to make it move away from you.
examples: She pushed the stroller up the path.
Push the button to start the machine.
He pushed the door open with his shoulder.

easy.def: A person who is easy to beat or talk into things.
examples: The puppy is a pushover for treats.
Our team was no pushover.
He is a pushover for hugs.

more.def: A person who is easily beaten or who gives in when asked.
examples: The other team was no pushover, and the game was close.
She is a pushover when her dog begs for food.
Dad is such a pushover when we ask for a story.

easy.def: An exercise where you lie facedown and push your body up with your arms.
examples: I did ten pushups.
A pushup is hard.
Do a pushup.

more.def: An exercise in which you lie facedown on the floor and push your body up with your arms and lower it again.
examples: I can do ten pushups in a row.
The coach made us do pushups.
A pushup works the muscles in your arms.

easy.def: Bossy and rude about getting what you want.
examples: The pushy boy cut in line.
Do not be pushy.
A pushy kid took the ball.

more.def: Too eager to get what you want, so that you push other people around or boss them.
examples: The pushy boy cut to the front of the line without asking.
Try not to be pushy when you ask for a turn.
The pushy seller would not take no for an answer.

easy.def: A cat.
examples: Here, puss, puss, puss!
The puss is sleeping.
I called the puss.

more.def: A word people use to call or speak to a cat.
examples: "Here, puss," she called, holding out a bowl of milk.
The old woman said hello to the puss on her windowsill.
In the story, Puss wore a pair of tall boots.

easy.def: To set something in a place.
examples: Put the cup on the table.
I put my coat on the hook.
She put the toy away.

more.def: To place something somewhere or to move it into a certain position.
examples: Please put your shoes by the door.
He put the cookies in a jar to keep them fresh.
We put a blanket over the sleeping baby.

easy.def: A gentle hit of a golf ball on the green.
examples: He made a putt.
The putt rolled in.
A long putt won the game.

more.def: A gentle stroke in golf that rolls the ball toward the hole.
examples: He made a short putt to win the game.
The ball rolled slowly after a gentle putt.
She sank a long putt on the last hole.

easy.def: To hit a golf ball gently toward the hole.
examples: He will putt the ball.
She putted from the edge.
Dad putts well.

more.def: To hit a golf ball gently so that it rolls toward the hole.
examples: She putted the ball across the smooth green.
Dad putts carefully before every shot.
He putted twice before the ball rolled in.

easy.def: To spend time doing small, easy jobs.
examples: Dad putters in the garden.
She puttered around the house.
I putter.

more.def: To spend time doing small, relaxing jobs in an unhurried way.
examples: Dad likes to putter around in the garden on Sundays.
She puttered about the kitchen making tea.
Grandpa puttered in the garage all afternoon.

easy.def: A soft, sticky stuff you press into holes.
examples: Dad used putty.
The putty is soft.
Putty fills the crack.

more.def: A soft, sticky substance that can be pressed into shape, used for fixing glass in a window or filling holes.
examples: Dad pressed putty around the window glass to hold it in place.
She filled the crack in the wall with putty.
Silly putty stretches and bounces.

easy.def: A game that tests how well you think.
examples: I like a puzzle.
We did a jigsaw puzzle.
The puzzle is hard.

more.def: A game or problem that you solve by thinking or by fitting pieces together.
examples: We did a jigsaw puzzle on a rainy day.
The word puzzle was hard.
She solved the puzzle in ten minutes.

easy.def: Confused and trying to work it out.
examples: She looked puzzled.
The puzzled dog tilted its head.
I was puzzled by the riddle.

more.def: Confused because you cannot work out an answer.
examples: The puzzled boy scratched his head at the riddle.
She looked puzzled when the clock stopped.
The dog tilted its head, puzzled by the strange sound.
